name: Renaissance Periodization (Dr. Mike Israetel)
who: Sport scientist (PhD) and RP co-founder; sells the RP Hypertrophy/Strength coaching apps plus direct 1:1 coaching.
why: One of the largest science-based coaching operations in fitness, backed by real academic credentials and a scaled subscription coaching-app business.
takeaway: Turn your training philosophy into a scalable coaching app — a system, not just personal attention.

name: Layne Norton (Carbon Diet Coach / Biolayne)
who: PhD in Nutritional Sciences and natural bodybuilder; co-founded Carbon Diet Coach, an adaptive AI nutrition-coaching app, after moving away from 1:1 coaching.
why: Built one of the first algorithm-driven science-based nutrition coaching products with a strong published-research background.
takeaway: Let an algorithm carry the coaching load once you can't scale 1:1 personally anymore.

name: Eric Helms (3D Muscle Journey)
who: PhD sport scientist, WNBF pro bodybuilder, and Chief Science Officer/co-founder of 3D Muscle Journey, which sells 1:1 coaching for natural bodybuilders and powerlifters.
why: Elite academic pedigree (research fellow, PhD mentor) paired with a small, well-regarded boutique coaching team.
takeaway: Stay small and boutique on purpose — a tight, credentialed team can outweigh sheer size.

name: Menno Henselmans
who: Physique scientist and former statistician; sells 1:1 online bodybuilding coaching under his own name (rebranded from Bayesian Bodybuilding).
why: One of the original pioneers of a formally 'evidence-based' individualized coaching method, with peer-reviewed co-authorship.
reach: IG approx 150K (follower count not independently confirmed this pass)
takeaway: Ground every coaching decision in individualized data — evidence-based means adapted to the person, not generic.

name: Barbell Medicine (Jordan Feigenbaum)
who: Physician (MD) and elite powerlifter; co-founded Barbell Medicine, which sells 1:1 and templated online coaching plus a training app.
why: Rare MD-plus-elite-lifter combination running a large, medically grounded strength-coaching organization.

name: Mike Tuchscherer (Reactive Training Systems)
who: Founder of Reactive Training Systems (RTS); sells RPE-based autoregulated online coaching for powerlifters.
why: Early pioneer of online powerlifting coaching, with 400+ lifters coached and multiple IPF world-record holders on his roster.
takeaway: Autoregulate by feel, not just fixed numbers — RPE-based coaching adapts to the lifter's actual day.

name: Bryce Lewis (The Strength Athlete)
who: Elite drug-free powerlifter (USAPL/IPF record holder); founded The Strength Athlete (TSA), an online powerlifting coaching group.
why: Competitive record backs a dedicated, longstanding powerlifting-only coaching business.
takeaway: Stay single-sport — a powerlifting-only coaching group backed by your own competitive record builds trust.

name: Sohee Lee (Sohee Fit)
who: PhD in Sports Science, CSCS; founder and head coach at SoheeFit Systems, running paid 1:1 online coaching since 2012.
why: Long-running, credentialed coaching practice with a strong, engaged female-focused audience.
takeaway: Stay in the coaching seat for over a decade — longevity itself becomes the credential.

name: Alberto Nunez (Team 3DMJ)
who: WNBF pro natural bodybuilder and Team 3DMJ coach, selling 1:1 natural bodybuilding coaching.
why: Competitive pro pedigree combined with membership in the well-regarded 3DMJ coaching collective.
takeaway: Join a well-regarded coaching collective — a respected team lends credibility no solo brand can buy alone.

name: Paul Carter (Lift-Run-Bang)
who: Bodybuilder/powerlifter with nearly 30 years in the field; founder of Lift-Run-Bang, an online coaching platform that has trained thousands of athletes.
why: Long track record coaching a large client base with a pragmatic, research-informed hypertrophy approach.
takeaway: Stay pragmatic — a research-informed but practical hypertrophy approach keeps thousands of clients training long-term.

name: Eugene Teo (Ganbaru Method)
who: Strength coach and content creator; founder of the Ganbaru Method app, which sells customized hybrid-training coaching programs with a coaching team.
why: Fast-growing paid coaching-app audience (200K+ claimed app users) built on a hybrid strength/bodybuilding method.
takeaway: Blend two disciplines into one named method — hybrid strength-and-bodybuilding drew a fast-growing paid audience.

name: Milo Wolf (Wolf Coaching / Stronger by Science)
who: PhD candidate in sport science and competitive natural bodybuilder; coaches clients through Wolf Coaching and as a Stronger by Science coach.
why: Active hypertrophy researcher (range-of-motion, lengthened partials) whose own findings feed directly into a real coaching practice.
reach: IG (@wolfcoach_) follower count not independently confirmed this pass, approx sub-100K
takeaway: Feed your own research findings directly into your coaching practice — test theory on real clients.

name: Ben Pakulski (Muscle Intelligence / MI40)
who: IFBB pro bodybuilder; founder of Muscle Intelligence, selling MI40 hypertrophy programs and M.I. Coaching (1:1 and group coaching).
why: Long-running bodybuilding coaching brand with a large legacy client base built on a biomechanics-driven training method.
reach: IG (@muscleintelligencepodcast) 34K; personal account count not independently confirmed this pass

name: Andrew Coates (Andrew Coates Fitness)
who: Coach with 23,000+ logged coaching hours; sells exclusive 1:1 online coaching with daily check-ins, program design, and nutrition guidance.
why: Deep hands-on coaching volume paired with a respected evidence-based industry podcast on the side.
takeaway: Log the hours — daily check-ins and deep hands-on coaching volume are what actually build the reputation.

name: Trevor Kashey (Trevor Kashey Nutrition)
who: PhD biochemist; founder of Trevor Kashey Nutrition, selling 1:1 'Cognitive Nutrition' coaching to individuals and fitness professionals.
why: PhD-level nutrition science applied through a scaled 1:1 coaching program with a claimed 12,000+ client history.
takeaway: Coach the coaches too — selling to fitness professionals multiplies the reach of your expertise.

name: Greg Nuckols (Stronger by Science)
who: Elite raw powerlifter and researcher; Stronger by Science sells premium 1:1 training and nutrition coaching from its own vetted coaches (e.g., Milo Wolf, Eric Trexler), on top of its free research writing.
why: One of the most respected research-to-practice media brands in fitness, with a real coaching bench behind the newsletter and podcast.
reach: Audience size not independently confirmed this pass (large newsletter/podcast following)
takeaway: Give away the research for free, then sell the vetted coaching bench behind it.

name: Jeff Nippard
who: YouTube science communicator and natural bodybuilder; sells structured, self-guided training programs (hypertrophy, powerbuilding) via jeffnippard.com — no personalized feedback or check-ins.
why: Reference-standard educational content and massive reach; coaching product is templated-only, so it clears the gate but sits at the bottom of the coaching-depth scale.
takeaway: Content can carry a business alone — a templated program still sells if the education is trusted.

name: Alan Aragon
who: Nutrition researcher and educator (30+ years); runs 1:1 nutrition consulting alongside publishing Alan Aragon's Research Review (AARR).
why: The longest-running evidence-based nutrition research review in fitness, paired with a genuine individual consulting practice.
takeaway: Publish a research review for decades — longevity in honest analysis outlasts any single trend.

name: Lyle McDonald (Bodyrecomposition)
who: Longtime evidence-based nutrition/training author; sells paid 60-minute 1:1 online consultations via bodyrecomposition.com rather than ongoing coaching.
why: Foundational figure in evidence-based fitness writing; the coaching product is a limited one-off consult, so it barely clears the gate.
reach: Reach not independently confirmed this pass (longtime niche following, no active mainstream social presence found)
takeaway: A single well-prepared consult can be the whole coaching product — depth over an ongoing retainer.
